title: Telling and writing stories
intro: Stories have characters and a place. A beginning introduces the situation, a middle shows what happens, and an ending tells what changes. Plan aloud before writing.
support: کیسه کرکټرونه او ځای لري. پیل، منځ او پای وګورئ. لومړی خپله کیسه ووایئ، بیا یې ولیکئ.
text:
Once upon a time, Sami packed a red bag.
At the park, he dropped his apple.
A friend found it and Sami said thank you.
model: First Sami packs. Next he drops the apple. Last the friend helps. A three-picture retelling could use one caption for each event. A short poem can use a repeating starter, such as “I see”.
activity: Draw three boxes for the story and write one sentence under each. Say a different ending, then write it.
adult: Listen for the main events in order without the text visible. Ask the child to say a plan, then write an original story or a two-line patterned poem.
adultPs: کیسه پټه کړئ او اصلي پېښې په ترتیب واورئ. ماشوم دې لومړی پلان ووایي او بیا خپله کیسه یا لنډ نظم ولیکي.

rounds.prompt: Put the event words in story order.
rounds.hint: Look at the first verb. The friend appears at the end.
rounds.instruction: انګلیسي پوښتنه ولولئ او برخې په ترتیب وټاکئ.

rounds.hint: Who packs the bag and drops the apple?
rounds.instruction: انګلیسي پوښتنه ولولئ او برخې په ترتیب وټاکئ.

rounds.prompt: Where does Sami drop the apple?
rounds.instruction: انګلیسي پوښتنه ولولئ او برخې په ترتیب وټاکئ.

tasks: Name the main character and draw where the middle happens.
Point to the first, middle and last events. Tell them aloud.
Draw a picture of the apple event and write a caption.
Draw three panels and retell the story using your own captions.
Say a different ending. Write one sentence that could finish the story.
Start an original story with Once upon a time. Plan three events aloud.
Write a two-line poem starting each line with I see. Read it to someone.
Retell Sami's story without the page. Draw three panels and label them.
Write an opening for a story about a child at home. Add a problem and an ending.
Write and read a two-line repeating poem about the park. Explain the pattern you used.
